featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a deeply disappointing and upsetting experience at Hospital Tulip, opposite Croma in Prabhadevi. The staff was extremely unprofessional, rude, and completely lacking in empathy.

I rushed my 2-year-old child to the hospital on 13th October at around 1:30 AM due to a very high fever. Instead of providing proper care, the staff behaved harshly and disrespectfully—not only toward my child but also toward us as parents. We were not allowed to accompany our own child, which was extremely distressing and unacceptable, especially in an emergency.

Inside, they handled her very roughly, kept scolding her, and showed no sympathy or understanding. They even forced her face down just to administer an injection, which was done very unprofessionally. No parent should ever have to witness—or be excluded from—such treatment.

To make matters worse, the hospital’s contact number is almost always busy, as if they’re constantly on another call, which added unnecessary stress during an already difficult situation.

Overall, this has been one of the worst medical experiences I’ve ever had. I would strongly advise against visiting this hospital. The staff is abrupt, disrespectful, and completely lacking in professionalism or basic empathy.

Extremely Disappointing Experience.

My experience at Ramakrishna Mission Hospital was deeply unsatisfactory and alarming. For an institution associated with such a respected name, the overall standards of care, hygiene, and management are far below acceptable levels.

The trainee doctors displayed an arrogant, careless, and dismissive attitude, lacking basic empathy and professionalism. Patient concerns were often brushed aside, creating unnecessary stress and frustration.

Cleanliness is a major issue throughout the hospital. Washrooms and patient areas were unhygienic, poorly maintained, and visibly dirty, raising serious concerns about infection control and patient safety.

Despite booking and paying for a “First Class” room, the condition was horrible and unacceptable—dirty floors, stained and broken tiles, poorly maintained toilets, foul smell, and an overall neglected environment. This was misleading and completely unworthy of a first-class facility.

Time management is extremely poor. Long waiting hours, lack of communication, and no respect for patients’ time indicate weak administration and poor coordination.

The only positive aspect of this hospital experience was the professionalism and dedication of Dr. Ulhas Nadkarni and Dr. Amarish Warty. Both doctors were knowledgeable, patient, and compassionate, and they treated us with respect and genuine care. Their conduct reflects what medical professionalism should look like.

Unfortunately, apart from these two doctors, the hospital suffers from poor hygiene, unprofessional trainee behavior, misleading facilities, and inefficient management. Immediate corrective action is required.

I would not recommend this hospital unless serious improvements are made.

We had an extremely distressing experience at Siddhachal Hospital, Prabhadevi, after our elderly family member was admitted there in an emergency with a fracture on her left hip. I would strongly advise against choosing this hospital, especially for elderly patients or anyone needing urgent, attentive care.

From the moment we arrived, the facility was poorly equipped, lacking even a decent waiting area. The treatment was abysmal — staff showed no understanding of pain management, administering painkillers randomly without clear guidance or monitoring. The response time was shockingly slow, and even basic infrastructure like Wi-Fi was dysfunctional, with internet speeds so slow that documentation took ages, directly delaying care.

Throughout our time there, staff were often seen gossiping instead of attending to patients, adding to the frustration and anxiety of an already difficult situation. When we decided to shift our grandmother to another hospital due to their incompetence, staff delayed the transfer unnecessarily, questioning our decision rather than focusing on a safe and swift discharge.

The ambulance service was unprofessional and unsafe:

We had requested to go to their Lower Parel branch, but were wrongly brought to Prabhadevi.

The ambulance staff had no clue how to properly lift a patient with a hip fracture, lacked the strength needed, and mishandled her during transfers.

The ambulance light kept flickering uncontrollably while going over speed bumps, creating an alarming and chaotic environment.

There was nothing positive about this experience. From slow internet hampering documentation to staff gossiping instead of caring for patients, every aspect of the stay was marked by carelessness, inefficiency, and a lack of empathy.

I strongly recommend avoiding Siddhachal Hospital, Prabhadevi. The hospital’s systems, infrastructure, staff training, and attitude are completely inadequate for providing safe and dignified care.

featured_reviews.name: Parag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.
